# Projected-extrema changed-case audit for #2840

Candidate: `09495e082`; exact main comparison base: `3f82278a14c1a6104db8e090a59b4bcf677ace01`.
Reference: pinned v1.0.1, `v1-3fd5b9548d19-726643fb17a52b7d`.
Unit: `curve.curve_p1`. All 45 cases below passed native parity on the base and differ on the candidate.
The generated inputs are reproducible from each case seed using that revision's runner.

For each polynomial/rational span, independently construct homogeneous coordinates
and the squared projected-distance numerator `A`; with weight polynomial `W`,
stationary candidates are real roots of `A' W - 2 A W'`. Compare these and interval
boundaries with every returned solution. The double-cross projection matrix is
`(N dot N) I - N N^T`. This calculation uses numerical polynomial roots in f64;
it is an independent numerical audit, not outward-rounded interval certification.
Positive control weights establish a positive denominator on the stored spans.
A 1,001-point-per-span diagnostic cross-check does not substitute for the polynomial calculation.

All 52 returned values meet `1e-9` relative accuracy without an absolute floor;
every returned candidate is within the original query distance tolerance of the
oracle. Each case includes an optimum within `1.07e-14` absolute of the oracle.
Extra All-mode answers may be within tolerance rather than exactly optimal.
This does not establish exhaustive All-mode enumeration or correctness of unchanged cases.
The comparison tolerance was not loosened and these are not native parity passes.

**Domain qualification:** `gen0975` requests `[9.11108388782278,11.50075760044348]`
with out-of-bounds evaluation enabled, but the cache ends at `9.828519172103537`.
Both implementations search stored spans only. The new answer is optimal on that
intersection, distance `2.3115157576033067`; polynomial continuation to the requested
upper endpoint has distance `7.817064617523855`. Extrapolated search semantics remain
unresolved; this row must not be presented as a complete repair of the requested-domain query.

`gen2419`, a permanent regression that failed the earlier candidate, now agrees
with the native result and is absent from this changed set.
